tickets.description: `skills._read_skill_description` swallows the error that a `SKILL.md` without frontmatter raises, so `kahnban skills list` shows such a skill with an empty description although the file has a heading or a first line that would do. Found by the coverage work on `skills.py`; `tests/test_skills_sources.py` records the empty result today.

tickets.title: Repeat the fast simulation five times on an unchanged tree and gate only the metrics that never move
tickets.description: The simulation baseline was made in one run and compared in one later run (docs/gap-fix-plan.md, G6). Two matching runs do not show that a metric never moves, and the tolerances in `tests/sim/compare.py` are guesses. A metric that moves on an unchanged tree would block every pull request. `python tests/run_sim.py stability` should run the chosen scenarios N times (default 5) on the same tree, report which metrics moved, and let `compare` skip those, so only metrics that never move are gated.

tickets.title: Break down status.json metrics per role: which worker caused the rejections
tickets.description: `status.json` metrics count verify attempts and rejections per ticket and give a board-level first-pass yield, but not who caused them. With several workers, or after changing one worker's prompt, nobody can tell which owner's work fails verify or gets rejected, or which reviewer rejects. The ticket Log already has what is needed: `claimed by <owner>` (and `taken over by <owner>`), `verify exit=N`, and `rejected by <reviewer>:`.

tickets.title: Rename the bundled blast-radius skill: it collides with the ticket field of the same name
tickets.description: The bundled skill `blast-radius` shares its name with the ticket field `## Blast radius`, so `/blast-radius` and the field are easy to confuse (the field is the files a coder may touch; the skill is a method for finding what a change breaks elsewhere). Rename the skill to `change-impact` (decided with the user, 2026-10-26) everywhere it is shipped: the bundle, `adapters/skills`, `.agents/skills` and the lock. Mentions of the ticket field stay as they are. The rename needs more files than the usual limit of 3, so `max_blast_radius_files` is raised for this one ticket and restored when it is done.

tickets.title: Tamper resistance for the frozen records: keep contract and approval records out of the workers' write access
tickets.description: Approvals are signed with a key kept outside the repository, but the frozen contract is not: `contract_hash` is plain frontmatter, so a worker that edits the acceptance criteria, blast radius or validation can write the matching hash too, and `verify_contract` passes. Sign the hash at the same moments it is written (`ready`, and the freeze at `claim`) with the existing key, store it as `contract_sig`, and check it wherever `verify_contract` runs. With `require_signed_approvals`, a hash without a signature is refused with the way out (`move` back to refining, then `ready`). Limit, to be stated in the README: a worker running as the same OS user can still read the key file, so this is a tripwire. Real isolation is a container or a separate OS user for workers, which is a deployment choice, not engine code.

tickets.title: Reviewer identity that is not self-asserted
tickets.description: `kahnban approve --reviewer <name>` records whatever name is typed. The owner check compares two strings, so a typo, a worker or a second hat can approve under any other name. Decided with the user (2026-10-26): registered reviewer keys.

tickets.title: Parallel workers in kahnban run (leases already allow it)
tickets.description: `kahnban run` drives one ticket at a time, so a board with several ready tickets waits on each coder in turn. Leases and the dispatcher's free-blast-radius rule already stop two coders from holding overlapping tickets. Decided with the user (2026-10-29): parallel implement only. `kahnban run --jobs N` runs up to N coder workers at once, each in its own worktree. Only the worker subprocess runs off the main thread; claim, verify, review, merge and done stay one at a time, so the merge queue, the board's commits and signing are unchanged. The default is 1, which behaves exactly as before. Limit: tickets with disjoint declared radii can still conflict at merge; the merge queue refuses those as it does today.

tickets.title: The default worker command cannot finish a ticket headlessly: claude -p with acceptEdits is asked to approve git and kahnban commands. Allow the commands each role needs (allowedTools or project permission rules written by skills install) and prove it with the live test
tickets.description: A headless `claude -p --permission-mode acceptEdits` worker is asked to approve `git add`, `git commit` and `kahnban approve`, and a headless worker cannot answer. Three live runs with Haiku (2026-10-25 and 26) and a probe show it: with nothing allowed the coder cannot commit; with the rules in the project's `.claude/settings.json` (`permissions.allow`) it still cannot, because a headless worker ignores them; with `--allowedTools` on the command line it can. So the rules belong in the worker command, which lives in `plans/board.config.json` where the adopter reviews it.
